A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same analytic bijections and radial-flow framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across the extensive reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original training results on one-dimensional densities, two-dimensional spiral and Gaussian-mixture targets, and phi4 lattice field theory.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds CIFAR10 and UCI evaluations, derivative-accuracy comparisons, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: V2 introduces and evaluates the spline+ hybrid: stacked sinh-conjugation bijections followed by a rational-quadratic spline. The three original analytic families, radial architectures, and zero-mode construction remain; renaming cubic polynomial to cubic conjugation does not change that method.

E1.justification: Section 5.4 adds image density estimation on CIFAR10 and tabular density estimation on POWER, GAS, HEPMASS, MINIBOONE, and BSDS300. This substantially expands coverage beyond the retained synthetic distributions and lattice field theory.

E2.justification: V2 adds a rational-quadratic spline baseline to the existing phi4 comparison and a spline variant to the layerwise spiral visualization. The new scalar smoothness and runtime studies also compare against splines. These extend participation of an existing comparator family.

E3.justification: New protocols include CIFAR10 bits-per-dimension evaluation, dataset-specific UCI training, a controlled 20,000-step comparison of 42 cubic bijections against three 14-knot splines, derivative-error evaluation, and isolated GPU timing. The earlier training budgets in v1 Table 3 remain in v2 Table 5.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 adds matched-density analyses of second-derivative accuracy and training-loss variability. Appendix B.5 extends the layerwise artifact analysis to spline coupling, and B.8 adds runtime scaling with stack count or knot count. Earlier radial, Fourier, and mode-collapse analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: V2 newly specifies that retained training curves use medians pooled across six seeds within 15-step or 50-step windows (Figures 12 and 15). Six-seed mean/standard-deviation reporting and three-run phi4 median/interquartile reporting remain. An increase in run counts is not established.

E6.justification: V2 adds CIFAR10 results of 3.36–3.37 bpd, UCI likelihoods, Fourier-flow NLL values, spline phi4 results, derivative-error ratios, and timing measurements. Table 3 shows spline+ improving over the reproduced spline on POWER, GAS, and BSDS300 but worsening on HEPMASS and MINIBOONE. Most earlier plotted results are retained.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 replaces v1's broad polynomial-degree argument with a denominator-degree argument and a general linear-over-quadratic rational form. Section 4.2 changes the stated origin-derivative condition from unity to an angle-independent constant and supplies explicit corrective-sinh parameters. The main inverse and Jacobian derivations remain.

C1.justification: The central analytic-invertibility, radial-efficiency, and mode-collapse claims persist. V2's conclusion adds claims about standard benchmarks and hybrid benefits, narrows artifact advantages to affine coupling on structured targets, and makes the coupling-flow smoothness guarantee conditional on smooth conditioner networks.

C2.justification: V1 describes bijection costs as negligible and makes broader coupling-artifact statements. V2 discusses application-dependent runtime overhead, acknowledges spline mitigation of folding, interprets UCI hybrid failures through overfitting, and explains derivative-accuracy benefits. These substantially develop the applicability boundaries and interpretation of the central advantages.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds CIFAR10 architecture and preprocessing details, including ActNorm, GELU conditioners, logit preprocessing, and deviations from published RealNVP. It also provides UCI-specific architectures and training settings. V2 newly mentions a tutorial notebook; the original numerical-stability and parameter-constraint details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 removes references including Midgley et al.'s SE(3)-equivariant flows and Draxler et al.'s coupling-universality work. It explicitly positions analytic bijections as complementary to equivariant and manifold architectures and clarifies its discrete-flow scope. The principal affine, spline, and radial-flow positioning remains.

P1.justification: V2 extensively condenses and rewrites the introduction, background, methods, and conclusion. Stacking and coupling move into the bijection section, radial flows become the focus of Section 4, and experimental explanations are redistributed across expanded appendices. Terminology is standardized around conjugation and stack count.

P2.justification: The main text changes to two columns with extensive figure resizing, recoloring, and relocation. The 1D summary becomes vertically stacked, and the Gaussian-mixture display becomes a 2-by-2 grid. V2 adds benchmark tables, derivative and runtime plots, and a spline panel to the layerwise visualization.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for general applicability and smoothness benefits through controlled UCI comparisons, matched-density derivative analysis, a spline physics baseline, and measured computational tradeoffs. These address important gaps in v1's predominantly synthetic/physics evaluation and qualitative smoothness arguments. CIFAR10's claimed matched-architecture gain remains confounded by architectural differences disclosed in Appendix C.6, but the other additions provide substantial independent improvements in evidential support.
